references.text: Nicodemus is mentioned again here as the one who had come to Jesus earlier. He speaks to the Pharisees and council members and defends Jesus by asking whether the law condemns anyone without first hearing them. See [ref:Joh 7:50-51|John 7:50-51].

Nicodemus is mentioned for the third time in the Gospel of John, where he brings a mixture of myrrh and aloes to anoint Jesus' body after the crucifixion. This shows the development of his relationship with Jesus. See [ref:Joh 19:39|John 19:39].

The Pharisees ask rhetorically whether any of the council members or Pharisees have believed in Jesus – precisely what Nicodemus, as a Pharisee and council member, was about to do. See [ref:Joh 7:48|John 7:48].
Many of the council members believed in Jesus but did not confess him openly for fear of the Pharisees – which may explain why Nicodemus came to Jesus at night. See [ref:Joh 12:42|John 12:42].

Joseph of Arimathea is described as a good and righteous member of the Council who was waiting for God's kingdom – a parallel to Nicodemus, who was also one of the Jewish council members and sought the truth from Jesus. See [ref:Luk 23:50-51|Luke 23:50-51].
Gamaliel was another Pharisee in the Council who showed openness toward the Christians, which recalls Nicodemus' attitude as a Pharisee and council member. See [ref:Apg 5:34|Acts 5:34].
